But he cannot afford to be caught in incidents in the midfield.“Race smart in the early stages tomorrow and I am sure he has the pace to climb his way back up the field,” said the Mercedes deputy team principal, Bradley Lord.Quick GuideAzerbaijan F1 qualifying timesShow1George Russell🇬🇧Mercedes1:42.5362Charles Leclerc🇲🇨Ferrari1:43.3633Oscar Piastri🇦🇺McLaren1:43.3644Isack Hadjar🇫🇷Red Bull1:43.5005Lando Norris🇬🇧McLaren1:43.6726Lewis Hamilton🇬🇧Ferrari1:43.8587Pierre Gasly🇫🇷Alpine1:44.0478Max Verstappen🇳🇱Red Bull1:44.0819Carlos Sainz🇪🇸Williams1:44.56610Franco Colapinto🇦🇷Alpine1:44.963Q2 eliminations11Oliver Bearman🇬🇧Haas1:44.77512Liam Lawson🇳🇿Racing Bulls1:44.86013Alexander Albon🇹🇭Williams1:45.00114Esteban Ocon🇫🇷Haas1:45.01615Arvid Lindblad🇬🇧Racing Bulls1:45.10616Kimi Antonelli🇮🇹Mercedes1:45.504Q1 eliminations17Gabriel Bortoleto🇧🇷Audi1:45.79918Nico Hülkenberg🇩🇪Audi1:45.920*19Fernando Alonso🇪🇸Aston Martin1:46.59320Sergio Pérez🇲🇽Cadillac1:46.658*21Lance Stroll🇨🇦Aston Martin1:47.33722Valtteri Bottas🇫🇮Cadillac1:48.920Alonso and Stroll will start 21st and 22nd because of power-unit penalties.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.In Monza, when Antonelli took a new engine and accrued grid penalties – an imposition still to come for Russell at some point – Mercedes had been hopeful he might come back as high as fifth and he bettered that with a win. Such is the pace of the Mercedes in Baku it is not inconceivable that he could go as high as second, if beating his teammate on this form may be a bridge too far.Indeed, Russell did everything that was required of him with a confidence and touch that he has lacked at points this season. He has been quick all weekend in Azerbaijan, outpacing his teammate, and qualifying proved one of his best performances.The pre-season favourite, the British driver has been on the back foot due to problems around the car’s energy deployment which left him frustrated and examining his own driving style. However, having said he intended to drive more instinctively, he came into the weekend confident and backed it up with an inch-perfect run in qualifying. If he can convert it on Saturday he will have at least kept his slender title hopes alive.View image in fullscreenGeorge Russell (centre), Charles Leclerc (left) and Oscar Piastri – first, second and third – pose after qualifying.Photograph: Ali Haider/EPARussell was initially pushed hard by the McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri but with the track evolving and grip at its peak his last hot lap was a belter. Enormously quick in the first sector, he continued to improve and finished in 1min 42.526sec. Norris locked up on his final lap at turn three and could manage only fifth. Piastri was third and Isack Hadjar fourth, with his Red Bull teammate, Max Verstappen, in eighth and Lewis Hamilton in sixth.Russell will take heart from his fifth pole this year, his first in Baku and his first since the Austrian GP but the serious business remains on Saturday. On both sides of the Mercedes garage.Explore more on these topicsFormula One 2026George RussellKimi AntonelliMercedes GPFormula OneMotor sportnewsShareReuse this content

title: Andy Robertson says players are ‘not to blame’ for Manchester City’s actions | Manchester City | The Guardian
description: The former Liverpool defender Andy Robertson believes Manchester City’s players should not be punished for the club’s ownership breaking Premier League fair play rules
Author: Ewan Murray
Headline: The former Liverpool defender Andy Robertson believes Manchester City’s players should not be punished for the club’s ownership breaking Premier League fair play rules
Content: Andy Robertson tussles with Gabriel Jesus in April 2022, a season when Liverpool finished as runners-up to Manchester City.Photograph: Carl Recine/Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenAndy Robertson tussles with Gabriel Jesus in April 2022, a season when Liverpool finished as runners-up to Manchester City.Photograph: Carl Recine/Action Images/ReutersManchester CityAndy Robertson says players are ‘not to blame’ for Manchester City’s actionsCity found guilty of breaching Premier League rulesLiverpool finished second to City in 2019 and 2022Ewan Murrayin LjubljanaFri 25 Sep 2026 16.16 EDTLast modified on Fri 25 Sep 2026 19.04 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe former Liverpool defender Andy Robertson believes trophy-winningManchester Cityplayers should not have their achievements diminished or removed because of the actions of the club’s ownership.Robertson was flying from a training camp in Spain to Slovenia with the Scotland squad when news emerged thatCity have been found guiltyof multiple breaches of the Premier League’s financial fair play rules. The Scotland captain, who regularly jousted with City during his nine years at Anfield from 2017, was taken aback when news of the upcoming verdict was put to him in Ljubljana.Manchester City guilty of breaching Premier League’s financial fair play rules – as it happenedRead moreWith the Premier League likely to penalise City heavily – it is understood the club intend to appeal against a guilty verdict – retrospective trophy removal has been cited as a potential punishment. Robertson made clear he sees little merit in that.“For me, the players showed they were good enough on the pitch,” said the 32-year-old. “I don’t know too much about the charges and stuff like that. But they had an incredible team, one that I loved battling against. I don’t think when it comes to these things that players are ever to blame. That’s all I can focus on”.Robertson’s formerLiverpoolmanager, Jürgen Klopp, said he would throw a party if City had silverware removed.Robertson, now at Tottenham, will win his 98th cap and move within four of the record held by Kenny Dalglish when Scotland face Slovenia in the Nations League on Saturday.Explore more on these topicsManchester CityLiverpoolnewsShareReuse this content

title: We Manchester City fans fear relegation and losing trophies … but club are bang to rights | Manchester City | The Guardian
description: Despite the club’s shocking attempts to legally filibuster the charges out of existence for the past three years, we’ve rightfully failed
Author: Simon Hattenstone
Headline: Despite the club’s shocking attempts to legally filibuster the charges out of existence for the past three years, we’ve rightfully failed
Content: ‘Is City’s guilty verdict itself unjust? Some fans will say yes – but some of us believe we’re bang to rights.’Photograph: Oli Scarff/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreen‘Is City’s guilty verdict itself unjust? Some fans will say yes – but some of us believe we’re bang to rights.’Photograph: Oli Scarff/AFP/Getty ImagesManchester CityWe Manchester City fans fear relegation and losing trophies … but club are bang to rightsSimon HattenstoneDespite attempts to legally filibuster the charges out of existence for the past three years, we’ve rightfully failedFri 25 Sep 2026 13.51 EDTLast modified on Fri 25 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTShareIt couldn’t have been more prophetic. In 2008, 15 years before Manchester City were charged with financial fraud, fans started singing “City’s going down with a billion in the bank” to the tune of Yellow Submarine. This was because the former Thailand president Thaksin Shinawatra’s 15-month ownership of Cityhad come to an abrupt endwhenmore than £1bn of his assets were frozen. And although Sheikh Mansour of the UAE had stepped in to save City, we were sinking fast.Despite the UAE’s untold riches, by December we were in the relegation zone. It’s called Cityitis – shorthand for our tendency to self-destruct when things appear to be going well. In fact we won trophy after trophy. But we continued to sing the song about going down with a billion in the bank. When the financial fair play investigation was launched in 2018, the chant got louder. Then in 2023 we learnedthere were more than 100 charges. The chant became even louder and more cavalier. And now that our grubby, griftin’, cheatin’ chicken hascome home to roost, you can bank on one thing (if banks still deal with us) – the chanting will be louder and more cavalier than ever.Manchester City found guilty of breaking Premier League’s financial fair play rulesRead moreAfter all, this is a club that believes schadenfreude starts at home. We brag about our failings. Other songs we sing include “Empty seats at home” (to the tune of the Beautiful South’s Rotterdam) because we can’t sell out our tickets and “Is This the Etihad?” (to La donna è mobile from Verdi’s Rigoletto, natch) at deathly quiet away grounds.It’s not about tempting fate. Nor is it hubristic irony – we can’t sell out despite winning all these trophies. It’s simply an acceptance that one way or another we’ll always be City, always suffer from Cityitis, and come the day, despite our endless UAE riches, we’ll do a City.And that day has come. We don’t know what our fate, or sentence, is yet. When Iinterviewed Wayne Rooneyrecently he suggested we would have 60 points docked, making it virtually impossible for us to avoid relegation.It could be worse, of course. We could lose all eight trophies we won in the period (2009-10 to 2017-18) we flouted fair play, including three Premier League titles and our record-breaking centurions season whenwe won with 100 pointsin 2017-18. To me, that would be disproportionate and would in effect mean the Premier League eating itself.But is the verdict itself unjust? City will say yes because they don’t want anything as petty as fair-play rules thwarting their bid for global domination. The lawyers will say yes because they’re paid to do so. Many fans will say yes because they’re fans. But some of us believe we’re bang to rights.Everton and Nottingham Forest have been docked points for lesser offences, so it would be embarrassing if City had got away with it; an undeniable case of one rule for the rich. Despite City’s shocking attempts to legally filibuster the charges out of existence for the past three years, we’ve rightfully failed. Although it appears this is not the end because City intend to appeal.View image in fullscreenThe 2017-18 Premier League title may be one of eight trophies that Manchester City fear losing.Photograph: Oli Scarff/AFP/Getty ImagesOur behaviour has been pretty outrageous at Dodge City. Failing to provide accurate and up-to-date financial reports, concealing salary details and bonuses, inflating sponsorship revenues and failing to cooperate or supply requested documents during the investigation all feature on the charge sheet. We used lawyers to royally take the piss. And when it comes down to it, that is not very City. After all, this is a club founded in 1880 as St Mark’s (West Gorton) by members of St Mark’s Church of England for humanitarian and social rescue purposes to serve the deprived area of east Manchester, where Shameless was filmed a century later.So what happens next? We may lose trophies. We will almost certainly get relegated. We almost certainly lose our best players and sayha det brato Erling Haaland, the great Nordic God of goalscoring (having said that he may stay just to see how many he could get in a Championship season). And we start building again.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionIf the very worst happens, and we lose all those trophies, at least we still have ouranni mirabileswhen we did the unprecedented domestic quadruple (2018-19), and treble including the Champions League (2022-23). There was barely a whiff of scandal in these years. We were simply obscenely wealthy, brilliantly run and managed by the world’s numero uno Pep Guardiola.And plenty of positives will come out of our disgrace. The biggest being that justice is done. But there is so much more. City may get to play in the Championship where we enjoyed some of our finest moments (“We’ve got Kevin Keegan 100 goals a season,” sung to the tune of Let’s All Do the Conga a mere 24 years ago). League One? Halcyon days. For City fans of a certain age and disposition, beating Gillingham in the playoff is our top footballing memory. League Two? Thrill of the unknown. The only way is up, as the song goes.Ticket prices come down, allowing regular civilians back into the Etihad. Prices become so low that we fill the ground. Fans begin to realise Wembley visits and winning trophies are to be treasured. Pep has already gone so there’s no danger of losing him. We learn some humility and stop coming over all sullen because we’ve only won the League Cup and FA Cup in one season.Perhaps the biggest positive is that rather than simply pulling out the chequebook and signing the world’s best, we learn to think imaginatively. I noticed the God of Bermudan goalscoring Shaun Goater this year left his job coaching Aston Villa Women. He’s only 56, never relied entirely on pace, and I bet he’s a free agent.Explore more on these topicsManchester CityFinancial fair playcommentShareReuse this content

title: Thomas Tuchel warns Cole Palmer about ‘missing way too many’ England camps | England | The Guardian
description: The head coach said before England host Spain in the Nations League that Cole Palmer’s latest withdrawal with a minor injury was a ‘missed opportunity’
Author: Jacob Steinberg
Headline: The head coach said before England host Spain in the Nations League that Cole Palmer’s latest withdrawal with a minor injury was a ‘missed opportunity’
Content: Thomas Tuchel said he is ‘not ready to focus on players who are not here’ when questioned on Cole Palmer’s absence.Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PAView image in fullscreenThomas Tuchel said he is ‘not ready to focus on players who are not here’ when questioned on Cole Palmer’s absence.Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PAEnglandThomas Tuchel warns Cole Palmer about ‘missing way too many’ England campsHead coach said latest withdrawal is ‘missed opportunity’England host Spain in Nations League on SaturdayJacob SteinbergFri 25 Sep 2026 14.00 EDTLast modified on Fri 25 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThomas Tuchel has thrown Cole Palmer’s England future into major doubt by questioning whether the Chelsea attacker wants to be part of his squad.England’s head coach did not hold back onPalmer’s latest withdrawalfrom international duty, warning that the 24-year-old has missed too many opportunities to play for his country. Palmer has only 14 caps and his decision not to join up with the squad this week, because of a minor muscular injury, caused disappointment given he wasleft out of Tuchel’s World Cup squadafter struggling with form and fitness last season.De la Fuente brings insatiable Spain to England knowing World Cup is not enoughRead moreTuchel has put a lot of store in team spirit and is clear about wanting commitment. The German has rarely been able to work with Palmer, who had earned a high-profile recall after making a strong start to the campaign, and did not go down the diplomatic route when it was suggested the former Manchester City player does not seem desperate to play forEngland. “Hard to argue against what you’re saying,” Tuchel said.The line came with a warning for Palmer. “He misses too many camps,” Tuchel said. “That’s the overall headline. We have a lot of invitations and he couldn’t make this one. It is what it is. I am not ready to focus on players who are not here. The players that are here have my full attention.“It is a missed opportunity. He [Palmer] misses too many opportunities. I don’t blame him for it. It is just a fact. He misses way too many camps with injuries, and I only want to rely on what I witness within my team, and for that you have to be in camp.”The idea of asking Palmer to join the squad to build connections did not cross Tuchel’s mind. “To bring someone and take away capacity from our physios, it’s not helpful,” he said. “This is about the guys who are here and this is where the energy goes.”England open their Nations League campaign by hosting Spain at Wembley on Saturday evening and Tuchel is not short of alternatives to Palmer. Morgan Gibbs-White was called up as Palmer’s replacement from a holiday in Dubai.View image in fullscreenCole Palmer played in all four of Chelsea’s Premier League matches before pulling out of the England squad with a minor injury.Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PA“It leaves us with Jude Bellingham, Morgan Rogers, Morgan Gibbs-White and Eberechi Eze,” Tuchel said. “All in camp. All desperate to be here. All available. And all ready to go, ready to stop a holiday after one day in Dubai.”Palmer, who has played in all of Chelsea’s Premier League games this season, was not the only player to withdraw. However Tuchel has no issue with Tino Livramento, who missed Newcastle’s win over Hull last weekend. Concerns over the withdrawals of Manchester United’s Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford were also brushed aside. Declan Rice, also unavailable, was given a pass. The Arsenal midfielder played through pain at the World Cup and has had a draining workload.“Every case is individual and if Declan calls me and explains to me and I actually see him play v Brighton, I see straight away on TV that something is off,” Tuchel said. “He just confirmed that impression. Every case is different and I knew from Marcus, I knew from Kobbie that they play with discomfort.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionEngland go into their game against the world champions hoping to make a statement after the disappointment of theirWorld Cup semi-final defeatby Argentina. There has been a lot of focus on English football’s DNA but Rogers argued that Tuchel’s side are capable of keeping the ball if they go 1-0 up against Spain. The pain of losing to Argentina lingers.“We’re definitely good enough to do it,” the Chelsea attacker said. “But there’s not many teams in the world who can do that, especially in a World Cup semi-final in that moment. I was on the pitch, I felt it, we’re doing everything we can not to let them score and sometimes that can be a negative thought.“It is about keeping that calmness and composure. As heartbreaking as it was, I’m hoping that experience will put me and the group in massive stead going forward, that in those situations we can remember how it felt when the whistle went in that game, of how the last half-hour [against Argentina] felt. It just felt a bit sour, the way it ended.”Rogers accepted that other forwards needed to lower the side’s reliance on Harry Kane and Bellingham for goals. “They’re not going to be here for ever,” he said. “They might not be here for a camp or whatever, and other people need to step up. Starting now, the World Cup is done.”Tuchel has a call to make at right-back, with Jarell Quansah competing with Trent Alexander-Arnold. The uncapped Alex Scott hopes to get the nod over Myles Lewis-Skelly and James Garner in midfield.Explore more on these topicsEnglandThomas TuchelnewsShareReuse this content

title: Nations League: Kylian Mbappé injured after scoring France winner in Turkey | Nations League | The Guardian
description: Victory in Zinedine Zidane’s first game in charge was marred by Mbappé’s injury, while Belgium spoiled Roberto Mancini’s Italy return
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Victory in Zinedine Zidane’s first game in charge was marred by Mbappé’s injury, while Belgium spoiled Roberto Mancini’s Italy return
Content: Kylian Mbappé goes down holding his left knee shortly after scoring for France in Izmit.Photograph: Ali Atmaca/Anadolu/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenKylian Mbappé goes down holding his left knee shortly after scoring for France in Izmit.Photograph: Ali Atmaca/Anadolu/Getty ImagesNations LeagueNations League: Kylian Mbappé injured after scoring France winner in TurkeyFrance beat 10-man Turkey 1-0 to start Zidane eraItaly 0-2 Belgium, Georgia 0-1 Northern IrelandPress Association, AFP and APFri 25 Sep 2026 17.35 EDTLast modified on Fri 25 Sep 2026 19.45 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleKylian Mbappé limped off with an apparent knee injury, moments after scoring France’s winner against Turkey in theNations Leagueon Friday.The Real Madrid striker rifled in a low shot in the 55th minute after he was set up by Michael Olise. Soon after his record-extending 67thFrancegoal, Mbappé sat on the ground and grimaced as he rubbed the area around his left knee.Turkey 0-1 France, Italy 0-2 Belgium, Georgia 0-1 Northern Ireland: Nations League – as it happenedRead moreThe new France head coach, Zinedine Zidane, replaced Mbappé with Désiré Doué. In an encouraging sight, he was able to walk off the field of his own accord – but Zidane said afterwards that he expects his captain to return to Real Madrid for treatment.“It’s not great. Unfortunately I think he [Mbappé] is going to have to go home. We don’t want to take any risks,” Zidane told French broadcaster TF1. “He overextended his knee while shooting. It’s not very encouraging.”Jules Koundé hit the post for France before Turkey were reduced to 10 men, goalkeeper Ugurcan Cakir sent off for handling the ball outside his area after Bradley Barcola had been played through on goal.Elsewhere in Group A2, Roberto Mancini’s second debut as theItalyhead coach ended with a barrage of boos as the Azzurri were beaten 2-0 at home byBelgium.Mika Godts marked his first competitive cap with a fine individual goal after 20 minutes at the Stadio Olimpico. Dodi Lukebakio’s powerful strike in the 69th minute put the visitors out of sight in a chastening first game for Mancini, who accepted the home fans’ frustration.“It will be even better in the end, when you reach the top,” he said afterwards. “This is quite normal, you lose and the fans are disappointed and angry, that is part of the game.”It was an encouraging start, though, for new Belgium coach Mark van Bommel, who said after the game: “I’m 100% happy and satisfied, but I understand there’s always room for improvement.” Belgium host France in their next match on Monday, while Italy travel to Turkey.View image in fullscreenDodi Lukebakio celebrates with the Belgium substitutes after scoring against Italy in Rome.Photograph: Image Photo Agency/Getty ImagesEarlier, Shea Charles scored a last-gasp winner after his brother Pierce saved Khvicha Kvaratskhelia’s penalty asNorthern Irelandbegan their Nations League campaign with a dramatic 1-0 win overGeorgiain Tbilisi.Pierce Charles guessed right to keep out a poor penalty from Kvaratskhelia in the 65th minute, having already made an excellent save to keep out Georges Mikautadze’s close-range shot earlier in the second half of their Group B2 game.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionAt the other end, Shea Charles had spurned the visitors’ best chances to score but, in the ninth minute of time added on, he scrambled home from Trai Hume’s cross, securing a first ever away win for Northern Ireland in the Nations League.There was a nervous VAR check for offside but eventually Shea Charles could celebrate just his second international goal. Although Northern Ireland left the pitch celebrating, there was a major blow in stoppage time as defender Dan Ballard pulled up clutching his hamstring.View image in fullscreenShea and Pierce Charles embrace after both played a key role in Northern Ireland’s win.Photograph: Tamuna Kulumbegashvili/APMichael O’Neill had been frustrated with several decisions from the referee, Orel Grinfeeld – not least the penalty, which came after Ballard and Luka Locoshvili tussled in the box and Grinfeeld was sent to the VAR monitor. Northern Ireland’s next opponents,Hungary, lost 1-0 toUkrainein Budapest thanks to Danylo Sikan’s goal.In Group B4,Swedensecured a 2-1 home win overRomaniawith Alexander Isak and Viktor Gyökeres both on target for Graham Potter’s side. In the group’s other game,Polandwere held to a goalless draw byBosnia and Herzegovinain Warsaw.In the third-tier Group C2, Milution Osmajic’s 86th-minute goal helpedMontenegrofight back to beatCyprusin Podgorica. The visitors led through Marcus Edwards’ goal on his international debut, but Nikola Krstovic levelled before Osmajic’s late winner.Armeniatop the group after beatingLatvia2-0 at home earlier on Friday.Explore more on these topicsNations LeagueFranceBelgiumNorthern IrelandSwedennewsShareReuse this content

title: Liverpool’s Cody Gakpo reflects on ‘tough summer … in football and life’ | Liverpool | The Guardian
description: Cody Gakpo has reflected on a ‘very tough’ summer that featured personal tragedy and the collapse of a transfer to Manchester City
Author: Nick Ames
Headline: Cody Gakpo has reflected on a ‘very tough’ summer that featured personal tragedy and the collapse of a transfer to Manchester City
Content: Cody Gakpo scores a stoppage-time equaliser for the Netherlands against Germany in the Nations League on Thursday.Photograph: Olaf Kraak/EPAView image in fullscreenCody Gakpo scores a stoppage-time equaliser for the Netherlands against Germany in the Nations League on Thursday.Photograph: Olaf Kraak/EPALiverpoolLiverpool’s Cody Gakpo reflects on ‘tough summer … in football and life’Gakpo’s second son died during pregnancy in JuneDutch winger almost left Anfield for Manchester CityNick Amesin AmsterdamFri 25 Sep 2026 12.00 EDTLast modified on Fri 25 Sep 2026 18.51 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleCody Gakpo has reflected on a “very tough” summer that ended with the collapse of a transfer to Manchester City, revealingLiverpoolchanged their minds about letting him join their top-flight rivals.The forward scored a superb stoppage-time equaliser to earn the Netherlands a 1-1 draw in Thursday’sNations Leaguegame against Germany, who are coached by his former club manager Jürgen Klopp. It continues a bright start to the season for Gakpo, who was an £80m target for City in August before talks stalled. Earlier in the summer he was struck by tragedy, announcing with his partner, Noa van der Bij, that their second son had died during pregnancy.Gakpo denies Klopp perfect start as Xavi’s Netherlands rescue draw against GermanyRead more“It was a difficult summer for me, and my family, and everything surrounding football and life,” Gakpo said, when asked whether he thought he was going to leave Liverpool. “I just let it come, and it ended how it ended.”It was put to Gakpo that Liverpool were willing to let him go before changing their minds. “Spot-on,” he replied. “I cannot choose. So then I have to just try to do what I’m good at, and that’s playing football. I can be very worried about everything that could happen, or that didn’t happen, or whatever, but that wouldn’t help the situation.“It’s a very long story. The summer was very tough regarding everything. So I just let everything be and see how it came and it worked out in this way.”Gapko has refused to sulk since the move to City broke down, scoring in Liverpool’s opening-weekend draw against Newcastle and in their Carabao Cup win over Spurs. He has also recorded five assists.“It’s not about my character,” he said. “I’m now at the point that I don’t mind, I just want to enjoy football with my friends, with my teammates. I want to enjoy my life and whatever happens, happens. If I have no control over the situation, I will not worry. So I just do my job with that.”Gakpo admitted he “could do much better than I did last year” in a disappointing season for Liverpool that ended with the departure of Arne Slot. His value at Anfield was underlined by Virgil van Dijk, his national-team captain and Anfield teammate, who sang Gakpo’s praises following his last-gasp volley.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“If people didn’t appreciate Cody before, personally I don’t understand it,” Van Dijk said. “But I think it was a no-brainer for us as a team and a club to keep him. There were talks but, in my eyes, you can’t let him go and that’s why I said it. He is a friend as well. Ours, please – let’s keep it that way.”Explore more on these topicsLiverpoolNetherlandsNations LeaguenewsShareReuse this content

title: Top European leagues heighten pressure on Infantino with call for major changes at Fifa | Fifa | The Guardian
description: The Premier League, Bundesliga, La Liga and Serie A have called for fundamental reform of Fifa, saying the organisation’s governance is ‘not fit for purpose’
Author: Matt Hughes
Headline: The Premier League, Bundesliga, La Liga and Serie A have called for fundamental reform of Fifa, saying the organisation’s governance is ‘not fit for purpose’
Content: Gianni Infantino said this week he had ‘never been more determined and committed’ to doing ‘what is right for the game’.Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PAView image in fullscreenGianni Infantino said this week he had ‘never been more determined and committed’ to doing ‘what is right for the game’.Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PAFifaTop European leagues heighten pressure on Infantino with call for major changes at FifaFour leagues says Fifa governance ‘not fit for purpose’They criticise ‘expansionism’ and want more inputMatt HughesFri 25 Sep 2026 05.28 EDTLast modified on Fri 25 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Premier League has joined forces with La Liga, Serie A and the Bundesliga to call for urgent governance reform at Fifa after theWorld Cup sell-off debacle(FFE) as Gianni Infantino prepares to seek a fourth term as president.Their strongly worded statement is the latest indication that Infantino’s willingness to hold an external governance review does not go far enough, after the Guardian revealed that several Fifa council members have rejected that proposal.Infantino under pressure to include abandoned World Cup sell-off plan in external Fifa reviewRead moreIn a thinly veiled attack on Infantino, the four biggest European leagues accused the Fifa president of promoting “exploitative ideas” which threaten the foundations of the global game. They also referencethe Folarin Balogun affairby calling for more checks and balances to ensure that “individual disciplinary matters remain demonstrably insulated from political interference”.There has been considerable tension between the leading European leagues andFifafor some time, particularly over the increasingly congested calendar, which has been exacerbated by the development of new competitions such as the Club World Cup.The lobby group European Leagues filed a legal complaint to the European Commission against Fifa two years ago, accusing it of abusive practices, which has since been extended to include the women’s game.“Football’s long-standing foundations have, in recent years, been threatened by a fundamental governance problem, whereby Fifa’s president has actively promoted exploitative ideas rather than safeguarding against them,” the statement read. “And while football’s stakeholders ultimately forced the withdrawal of the Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme, the conditions that led to FFE remain.View image in fullscreenFolarin Balogun was allowed to play against Belgium despite being sent off in the USA’s previous match, against Bosnia and Herzegovina.Photograph: Christopher Torres/EPA“The Fifa president has now acknowledged the need for reform, but it is not enough for surface-level, process changes to be explored in the aftermath of FFE. Fundamental governance reform is essential to restore clear constitutional boundaries within Fifa, including confidence that individual disciplinary matters remain demonstrably insulated from political interference.“The future of Fifa matters to everyone who cares about football, because our sport cannot grow globally if its foundations are undermined.”In addition to condemning Infantino, the leagues called for three governance changes to be endorsed by the next president: the creation of a permanent decision-making body within Fifa including representatives of national associations, leagues, clubs and players; a commitment to publish the reasoning behind major decisions in advance; and the separation of Fifa’s regulatory functions from its commercial operations.“A Fifa governance that concentrates unchecked regulatory, commercial and political power in a single office, while relegating affected stakeholders to mere advisory status, is not fit for purpose,” the statement added.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“At this crucial time for our sport, we encourage candidates for the Fifa presidency to endorse these principles and, within the first 100 days of the next presidential mandate, to convene an independently chaired governance convention representing member associations and the wider football community, mandated to report publicly within six months.“All candidates for the Fifa presidency should publish their own reform programme, debate its contents and adhere to fair election rules. Fifa’s financial, legal, communications and marketing resources, as well as its football development funds, must remain strictly neutral and never create an electoral advantage for any candidate.”The deadline for presidential candidates declaring their intention to stand is 18 November, with the election in March.Infantino is the only declaration to date, with the Guardian reporting this week that there aregrowing concerns within European footballthat he will end up being re-elected unopposed.Explore more on these topicsFifaGianni InfantinoPremier LeagueFootball politicsBundesligaLa LigaSerie AnewsShareReuse this content

title: Rodri insists Manchester City ‘deserved’ success despite FFP guilty verdict | Manchester City | The Guardian
description: The Spain midfielder, who ended a glittering spell with Manchester City in the summer, said: ‘I believe in the justice system and innocence of the club’
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The Spain midfielder, who ended a glittering spell with Manchester City in the summer, said: ‘I believe in the justice system and innocence of the club’
Content: Rodri defended his former club Manchester City during a press conference to preview Spain’s Nations League match against England.Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenRodri defended his former club Manchester City during a press conference to preview Spain’s Nations League match against England.Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/ReutersManchester CityRodri insists Manchester City ‘deserved’ success despite FFP guilty verdict‘I believe in the justice system and innocence of the club’Midfielder ended glittering spell with City this yearPress AssociationFri 25 Sep 2026 18.42 EDTLast modified on Fri 25 Sep 2026 19.17 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRodri says nobody can take away Manchester City players’ success and still believes in his former club’s innocence despite reports they have beenfound guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules.The football world was rocked on Friday afternoon when a variety of outlets reported that the club had been found guilty on all but one of the 115 charges laid by the league in February 2023.Andy Robertson says players are ‘not to blame’ for Manchester City’s actionsRead moreCity have always strenuously denied the charges and a spokesperson said that “significant elements” of their legal case with the Premier League are still to be completed.Rodri ended his medal-laden spell at the Etihad Stadium in the summer and did not avoid the topic at a press conference on Friday evening previewing Spain’s Nations League opener against England.“We have faced something similar back in 2020, we had a similar judicial process,” the Barcelona midfielder said. “Different accusation but similar process.“There as well in the first instance we were found guilty, but we believed in the club and the innocence that the club maintained and in the end we ended up acquitted. So, I believe in the justice system, and I believe in the innocence of the club.”Rodri was referencing how City successfully overturned a two-year ban from European football imposed by Uefa after an appeal to the court of arbitration for sport.But the potential for sanctions in this case could be severe, raising questions about the club’s achievements – some of which were achieved at Wembley, where he spoke on the eve of the England game.View image in fullscreenRodri with then-manager Pep Guardiola after his goal won Manchester City the Champions League in 2023.Photograph: Molly Darlington/ReutersAsked if such talk hurts having achieved so much with City, Rodri said: “For us, the players, it is a different thing than for you guys. I can understand all kind of opinions, and it is something that now is big.“But we always tried to think in a positive way, when you live that club daily and the people who have worked hard all these years to have all the success we had.“Not only Pep [Guardiola] and the players but all the structure, from the owners to the guys who worked daily. What we did, they cannot take it out of us. It is something that is not paid by money, it is paid with effort, with partnership and with being shoulder to shoulder every day.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“We had a lot of success over the years and here in Wembley, so I can tell you everything was deserved and I’m glad I could live one of the best eras of English football.”Rodri seemed unruffled by Friday’s news and retains faith in the City hierarchy. “No, they always tell us the confidence they have on their innocence and when you look [in] to someone’s eyes and talk in that way,” he said.“We have the example of 2020 that the process was the same, and at the end nothing happened. We were very calm in this way. You never saw the team nervous about these kind of things.“Nowadays I’m not saying it’s going to say normal, but many teams or some teams go through these kinds of situations, and it’s part of football today. Everyone has to follow the rules, and for me that’s great.“But they always expressed the confidence that they never did something wrong, and we believe in that. That’s the thing. Until the moment they are proved wrong, we believe in the club. I’ve been there, I know how they work, and how they cooperate.”Explore more on these topicsManchester CityFinancial fair playnewsShareReuse this content

title: Manchester City guilty verdict ‘a historic decision’, says whistleblower Rui Pinto | Manchester City | The Guardian
description: The Football Leaks founder, who lives under police protection, exposed thousands of documents that triggered investigations into the club’s finances
Author: Miguel Dantas
Headline: The Football Leaks founder, who lives under police protection, exposed thousands of documents that triggered investigations into the club’s finances
Content: Rui Pinto, a Portuguese national, was arrested and tried in Budapest in 2019 for his alleged role in Football Leaks, and has since been tried – and acquitted – again.Composite: Manchester City FC/AFP via Getty Images; Manchester City FC via Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenRui Pinto, a Portuguese national, was arrested and tried in Budapest in 2019 for his alleged role in Football Leaks, and has since been tried – and acquitted – again.Composite: Manchester City FC/AFP via Getty Images; Manchester City FC via Getty ImagesManchester CityManchester City guilty verdict ‘a historic decision’, says whistleblower Rui PintoFootball Leaks founder’s information triggered probesHas faced legal issues and lives under police protectionMiguel DantasFri 25 Sep 2026 16.27 EDTLast modified on Fri 25 Sep 2026 19.02 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleYears afterhis leaks shook the foundations of European football, Rui Pinto is claiming vindication following Manchester City’s conviction for financial fair play breaches. The ruling has once again put the controversial whistleblower and his extraordinary archive of documents in the spotlight.Pinto, whose leaks of private documents helped trigger investigations into Manchester City’s financial affairs, has spoken about the club’s recent conviction for breaching financial fair play rules in a statement sent to the Guardian andlater posted on social media.Everything you need to know about Manchester City’s hearing and chargesRead moreCalling the conviction a “historic decision for English football”, Pinto said the ruling vindicates the vast repository of internal emails and financial records he leaked, material that helped trigger investigations by both Uefa and the Premier League.According to Pinto, the findings demonstrate thatManchester Citydid not simply bend financial fair play regulations, but systematically undermined them through what he described as “structural manipulation and financial manoeuvring”, reducing the governing rules to a “mere formality”.“That meticulously orchestrated fraud will finally be subject to punishment, and the impact will not merely be turbulent, but truly devastating for the Cityzens,” he said. Manchester City maintain their innocence andare expected to appeal.Pinto, a self-taught computer enthusiast, is the central figure behind Football Leaks, the platform that exposed millions of confidential documents linked to some of the biggest clubs, players and organisations in world football. His disclosures provided journalists with unprecedented access to the inner workings of the sport, while also placing their source at the centre of a major criminal investigation.Among the material Pinto provided wasinformation concerning Manchester City’s finances, which was passed to the German publication Der Spiegel and its partners in the European Investigative Collaborations network. The cache contained more than 70 million documents and ultimately contributed toa series of investigations and revelationsthat reached far beyond Manchester City. The disclosures touched on subjects ranging from allegations concerningCristiano Ronaldo and Kathryn Mayorgato the plans forthe proposed European Super League.View image in fullscreenKhaldoon Al Mubarak (right), the Manchester City president, holds several positions in the government of Abu Dhabi, whose royal family head City’s majority owners.Photograph: Jean Catuffe/Getty ImagesPortuguese national Pinto was arrested in Budapest in 2019 as part of an investigation into alleged attempted extortion and several cybercrimes. Following a lengthy trial, he was sentenced to four years in prison, with the sentence suspended.Pinto spent around a year in pre-trial detention, from March 2019 to April 2020,before being releasedafter reaching a cooperation agreement with the Portuguese authorities. For more than a year, investigators had sought access to hard drives containing information gathered through Football Leaks. The encryption used by Pinto had kept the devices inaccessible.In 2020, Pinto became a protected witness in Portugal in exchange for granting thePolícia Judiciária– the country’s criminal investigation police – access to the hard drives and assisting with a number of investigations. He remains under police protection and has lived in safehouses, with his current whereabouts kept confidential.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe RecapThe best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenRui Pinto’s supporters held a candlelit vigil for him in Lisbon while he was in pre-trial detention.Photograph: Mário Cruz/EPAIn Portugal, Pinto has becomea deeply divisive figure. To some, he is a whistleblower who exposed wrongdoing in an industry long criticised for its lack of transparency; to others, his methods crossed legal and ethical boundaries. Pinto has openly acknowledged his support for Porto, but that allegiance did not prevent him from leaking documents concerning the club and the dealings ofits former president, Jorge Nuno Pinto da Costa. Other major Portuguese clubs, including Benfica and Sporting, also appeared in material obtained through his activities.The scope of the leaks extended beyond football clubs. Judges, lawyers and politicians were among those whose information was exposed, demonstrating the extraordinary breadth of the material Pinto had collected.Nothing appeared to be entirely off-limits. Among the millions of documents gathered through his activities were files that shed light on the business interests and financial dealings surrounding Isabel dos Santos, the daughter of the former Angolan president José Eduardo dos Santos. The revelationsbecame known as Luanda Leaksand were investigated by journalists around the world, bringing renewed scrutiny to the wealth and business networks surrounding Angola’s former first family.Pinto wasrecently acquitted in a second trialin which he faced 241 charges relating to his activities as the source behind Football Leaks. While the acquittal removes one major legal threat, it remains unclear whether he will face further criminal proceedings connected to the millions of documents obtained and disclosed through the project. The possibility of additional cases means that, despite his cooperation with Portuguese authorities and his status as a protected witness, Pinto’s legal troubles may not yet be over.Explore more on these topicsManchester CityFinancial fair playFinancesBusinessnewsShareReuse this content

title: Warwickshire close on title as Somerset hopes fade: county cricket final round, day two – as it happened | County Championship | The Guardian
description: Warwickshire are seven wickets from victory over Leicestershire and only need a draw after Somerset toiled against Surrey
Author: James Wallace
Headline: Warwickshire are seven wickets from victory over Leicestershire and only need a draw after Somerset toiled against Surrey
Content: 14.26 EDTWarwickshire close on title, Kent lead promotion raceJames WallaceWarwickshiremade serene progress towards a ninth county championship title on a cloudy day at Edgbaston. A delay for autumnal mid-morning bad light in Birmingham curtailed their progress briefly in the first session but captain Ed Barnard and Sam Hain were as unbothered by the lingering nimbus as they wereLeicestershire’s bowlers.Barnard fell caught behind for 88 but Hain was the last man out for 142. Ethan Bamber and Chris Woakes struck in fading light to leave Leicestershire 55-3 and still adrift by 192 runs. A third two-day victory in a row was kiboshed by early evening gloom but Saturday will surely seeWarwickshireclinch the 2026 trophy.Somerset’s slim title hopes fizzled like flat cider in Taunton, their failure to take a third bowling bonus point asSurreyamassed 422 meant that Warwickshire can draw and still take the spoils.Last season’s winnersNottinghamshirereducedYorkshireto 179 all out in their first innings. Olly Stone sent Jonny Bairstow’s middle stump for the sort of cartwheel Simone Biles would be proud of as he took five wickets at Trent Bridge. However, bad news filtered through in the afternoon that Stone was injured – reportedly a hamstring – and it was serious enough for him to be immediately withdrawn from the match.Asa Tribe fell short of a double century in Cardiff but his 184 helpedGlamorganamass 505 in their first innings againstEssexwho then collapsed at the foot of the mountain on 100 for seven.Sussexare well on top ofHampshireat Southampton, Jaydev Unadkat’s five for 32 saw the home side skittled for 128 in response to 244.In Division Two, a defiant century from Ben Compton at Canterbury kept Kent’s promotion prospects in the balance as they made 353 and then took twoGloucestershirewickets to leave the visitors 63 runs shy.Fellow promotion chasersNorthamptonshirefought back to 249 for seven againstMiddlesexbut a slender lead of 97 runs will need to thicken on the hob if they are to set a challenging chase.Durhamdefied some mizzly Manchester weather andLancashire’s bowlers to post 493 in their first innings.Worcestershireare in control againstDerbyshire,where a fourth-innings chase of over 300 already looks out of reach.ShareUpdated at15.52 EDT

title: Mauricio Pochettino regrets not being ‘more involved’ with Balogun decision | USA | The Guardian
description: The comments are the most direct Pochettino has made regarding the Balogun situation since the World Cup
Author: Pablo Iglesias Maurer
Headline: The comments are the most direct Pochettino has made regarding the Balogun situation since the World Cup
Content: The US crashed out of the World Cup with a loss to Belgium in the last 16.Photograph: Alex Grimm/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenThe US crashed out of the World Cup with a loss to Belgium in the last 16.Photograph: Alex Grimm/Getty ImagesUSAMauricio Pochettino regrets not being ‘more involved’ with Balogun decisionUS striker had red card ban suspended for Belgium gameTrump said he called Infantino asking for reviewCoach says ‘energy of everything’ changed in momentPablo Iglesias MaurerFri 25 Sep 2026 11.02 EDTFirst published on Fri 25 Sep 2026 05.00 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleUS men’s national team head coach Mauricio Pochettino has said he regrets not being “more involved” in the situation surrounding US forward Folarin Balogun at this summer’s World Cup.Balogun was given a red card after a challenge against Bosnia and Herzegovina defender Tarik Muharemovic, which by rule is accompanied with a one-game suspension. Balogun’s ban for the next game against Belgium was suspended after the US Soccer Federation andDonald Trump lobbied Fifa, with Trump saying that he personally placed a call to Fifa president Gianni Infantino to ask the ruling be reviewed. Infantino maintains that the decision to reinstate Balogun was made independently by Fifa’s disciplinary committee.The entire affair cast a pall over what had been an otherwise positive tournament for the US to that point. Belgium’s players and coaches said in the wake of the decision that it provided extra motivation ahead of the match. Balogun himselflater spokeof having felt uncomfortable with the attention the situation placed upon him.Cavan Sullivan in, Christian Pulisic out: takeaways from the latest USMNT rosterRead moreSpeaking with broadcaster Andrés Cantor on Thursday, Pochettino said he was not involved in the decision – though in retrospect, he may have preferred to be.“Maybe I regret not having been more involved,” Pochettino saidin the Spanish-language interviewfor Fútbol de Primera. “In the situation that later generated all of the negativity afterwards. Maybe I regret not having been more inside of that decision making process. I wasn’t involved in that decision, to overturn the red card. As a football person, I understand everything … Beyond whether we were right or not [about the call on the field], I think nobody understood how it happened.”The US were thoroughly outclassed by Belgium in the 4-1 loss, beaten badly in every phase of play. In his remarks to Cantor, Pochettino suggested that the backlash surrounding the Balogun situation actively contributed to the loss.“As a football person,” Pochettino said, “where many times we have that emotional intelligence – [we know] that energy can change things. I think that energy changed the minute that happened. And by then, the game is played under different parameters, and that match was never a match where I believe the tactics, strategy, or selection of players would have changed the course of what happened during the game.”Pochettino also suggested that the group who participated in US Soccer’s efforts to get Balogun on the field against Belgium may have been too large for his liking.“That’s something we’ve talked about internally,” Pochettino said. “I think that these types of things have to be managed under a much more limited structure, a structure where decisions have to be made by very few people, where very few people manage these types of things. [Those decisions] should be strictly sporting and common sense, beyond whether a rule or a committee can say one thing or another.”Pochettino echoed those sentiments on Friday in comments to reporters in Orlando, where the USMNT will face Peru on Saturday.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Twice weeklySign up toSoccer DeskJonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“In the moment I didn’t understand the criticisms well, but now with time, I can see that you have to learn from mistakes and I think at times the things that happen in a tournament have to stay there,” he said. ‘“It’s good that laws and rules can allow you to change decisions, but because I’m coming from South American soccer and elsewhere, and we have such a tremendous respect for referees – if a ref is confused for a moment, he’s confused, and he the player pays for it. I also understand that you have to have the humility to understand that once in a while, you can be in the wrong. I think my error was to not be more involved in that moment. Things happen and in reality the energy of everything changed. That match is hard to analyze because it was created in an environment that wasn’t the best one as far as competing in a World Cup.”The coach also said he was unhappy with the decision for the US to play four games during this international window, calling it a “big risk”. The Americans face Chile on Tuesday in St Louis before traveling again to play Mexico outside Phoenix on 3 October and then Canada in St Paul on 6 October.“Plenty of other countries play only three this window. I think it’s a big risk, because from tomorrow there isn’t any time to rest, lots of travel too. We weren’t involved in that planning. We understand it’s a big risk, lots of players bring from preseason or early season in Europe and lots of MLS players are in a crucial moment at MLS,” he said. “I’d have preferred to have much more space between games to help the guys grow in the way we want for the future.”Explore more on these topicsUSAUS sportsWorld Cup 2026newsShareReuse this content

title: The comedians turning AI anxiety into punchlines: ‘It’s so good, it’ll completely alter our grasp on reality’ | AI (artificial intelligence) | The Guardian
description: Across videos, standup and cartoons, humorists are skewering big tech’s attempt to make AI ubiquitous and inevitable
Author: Matthew Cantor
Headline: Across videos, standup and cartoons, humorists are skewering big tech’s attempt to make AI ubiquitous and inevitable
Content: ‘[The comedy] effectively punctures tech CEOs’ relentless narrative: that artificial intelligence represents humanity peaking.’Photograph: marwanshaffey/alberta.tech/the_varunrana/theharrisaltermanView image in fullscreen‘[The comedy] effectively punctures tech CEOs’ relentless narrative: that artificial intelligence represents humanity peaking.’Photograph: marwanshaffey/alberta.tech/the_varunrana/theharrisaltermanAI (artificial intelligence)The comedians turning AI anxiety into punchlines: ‘It’s so good, it’ll completely alter our grasp on reality’Across videos, standup and cartoons, humorists are skewering big tech’s attempt to make AI ubiquitous and inevitableMatthew Cantorin Los AngelesFri 25 Sep 2026 08.00 EDTLast modified on Fri 25 Sep 2026 08.03 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on Google“Best case scenario, we never have to do any admin again,” saysan AI CEO. “Worst case, we all die.”A young manstruggles to the top of a beautiful mountain, words echoing in his ears: “AI will most likely lead to the end of the world, but in the meantime, there will be great companies created.” At the top of the mountain, he triumphantly holds up a sign: “Build a datacenter here.”On the New York subway, posters herald what appear to be AI startups. “What if forks were spoons?” asks an ad for Cutlery.ai. Another advises viewers that Ziplink is now known as Froggle.The posters are real, but the companies aren’t; the CEO and datacenter scenarios are social media sketches (though the “great companies” quote is agenuine piece of wisdomfrom Sam Altman). It’s all part of a recent wave of comedy inspired – but absolutely not generated – by AI.The comedy extends across all forms of media: social videos,standup,songs,humor columns,comic stripsandart installations. It takes aim at companies’ attempts to make AI ubiquitous, thedangers of believingits every word, its threats to society and the environment. It effectively punctures tech CEOs’ relentless narrative: that artificial intelligence represents humanity peaking; that it is inevitable and all-powerful; that we have no idea where it’s going and it could kill us all, but for some reason it is absolutely essential to pursue.Allow Instagram content?This article includes content provided byInstagram. We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as they may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content,click 'Allow and continue'.Allow and continueIt’s no surprise that a topic as pervasive as AI in 2026 would end up in comedians’ crosshairs. A MarchGallup pollfound 79% of Americans believe AI will reduce jobs. In aCNN pollthis week, 81% of respondents said they were more concerned than excited about how the technology could “fundamentally change our way of life”. Only 11% of Americans would support the building of a datacenter locally, according toUMass Amherst. Meanwhile, a handful of impossibly wealthy weirdos wander between podcasts and conference stages boasting about their plans to fundamentally alter what it means to be human.One way to expose the absurdity of the AI companies’ story is by exposing the flaws in their products.Ty Eveland, for instance, trolls AI doctors and HR professionals – the video bots you might awkwardly encounter at a virtual doctor’s appointment or job interview. Asked about marketing, he tells one bot interviewer he takes “everything with a grain of salt and maybe a little bit of pepper”. The bot, portrayed as a generically handsome blond man, responds earnestly: “When you say you take things with a grain of salt and pepper, what does that actually mean for a brand’s social media strategy?”If bots are approaching superintelligence, this one has clearly been left behind.35:15Can you stop AI datacenters? Comedian Charlie Berens thinks so – Stateside with Kai and CarterOther comedians parody the user experience: the comedian Aya Huseen, repeatedly popping out from behind a door,personifiestech companies’ desperate attempts to get users hooked on new AI features: “You sure you don’t want to try it with AI?” “This would be so much funner with AI.” “Just try generating it with AI.” The comedianTom Nestor imagines“how people who love AI think we see them,” telling a friend on the phone: “Do you know what I also really like? It’s not so good now but in years to come it’ll get so good that it’ll just completely alter people’s grasp of reality.” Inthe Atlantic, the humorist Alexandra Petri recounts a dream in which everything in her life has pivoted to AI, from children’s books – Goldilocks and the 4.5 Bears – to her cereal, which features “subtle changes in the recipe, such as the nuts now being the hard, metal kind”.Pro-human comedians have also taken aim at AI’s artistic pretensions. “If you are somebody who uses ChatGPT to generate videos, images, art, text, in an artistic capacity, to write for you, you are not somebody who deserves to be taken seriously,” said the comedian Caleb Hearon in a serious momenton his podcast. Acomic striptitled “AI Design Logic” puts it more succinctly: “Get me a cheese pizza,” a diner tells a waiter. When the pizza arrives, the customer takes credit, exclaiming: “Wow, look what I made!” It’s simple, scathingly effective, and highly meme-able. Even more succinct isa T-shirt wornby the actor Ayo Edebiri: “Do not talk to me about AI. I will kill myself.”double quotation markThe message that I want people to take home is to actually understand what they’re asking AI [and] what the limitations of it areAlberta DevorThe Altmans and Musks of the world may be louder than these comedians, but the collective weight of their jokes provides a counterbalance to the pro-AI declarations. “I would like to think that some of these [companies] are looking at the ridiculousness of where we’re at” and might be swayed by the success and relatability of comedy mocking their products, saysMarwan Shaffey, whose videos include a takedown of a water-guzzling Google in 2026, with its Gemini-generated search resultsthat are more about vibes thanaccuracy. “It does seem like the sentiment is changing, but I think it will take time.”Comedy, of course, can cut through the noise in a way that serious lectures may not. That has been the experience of Alberta Devor, who spent six and a half years as a software engineer at Google. Inone recent video, she offers a cool hack for when someone asks you a tricky question: instead of pulling out your phone and asking AI, it’s actually possible to use the LLM in your brain to produce a response. When a colleague wonders what “EOD” means, she immediately tells him. “How’d you ask Claude that so fast?” he asks. “I trained a model in my head,” she replies. “I just consumed a lot of media, a lot of books.”Allow Instagram content?This article includes content provided byInstagram. We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as they may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content,click 'Allow and continue'.Allow and continueDevor herself is a regular AI user. Still, she’s concerned about overreliance on the products, whether they’re being used to seek information or to code. “The message that I want people to take home is to actually understand what they’re asking AI, to actually understand what the limitations of it are,” she says in an interview. Her serious videos on these topics often meet with some backlash.Comedy, she says, tends to find a more open audience. “It makes people want to engage more, and then you can start to get through to these more complex ideas,” she says. “Like maybe we should be using our brain.”Not all the AI takedowns are themselves digital. The New York subway signs are the brainchildren of two comedians, Harris Alterman and Dave Ross, who designed a campaign mocking the inscrutable – and insufferable – language of bus-stop tech ads and San Francisco billboards.View image in fullscreenA fake tech subway ad by Harris Alterman and Dave Ross.Photograph: Harris Alterman/Harris Alterman and Dave Ross“It was the quickest writing and creative process I’ve ever had,” Ross said. The tech advertising tropes were so clear, and so different from how any human has ever talked, that it was easy to satirize. “We made a big Google Doc of every keyword from all these things – ‘agents’, ‘democratize’ – and then we made 50 frameworks of these ads”: “finally, X that you can Y, or from X to Y in just one Z”. They rearranged and filled in the frameworks, Mad Libs-style, and had them printed.Initially, the concept just seemed funny. “The more I talk about this, and it’s been months now, the more I realize just how disgusted I am with it,” Ross says of the ads’ language, which is “borderline offensive to the human brain”.Feeling overwhelmed by the AI doom loop? Here’s the essential reading list to make sense of it allRead moreOther comics are equally clear-eyed in their message, and more direct in their advocacy. The British comedian Cody Dahler, condemning “techy tits” such as Palantir CEO Alex Karp, AKA “evil Art Garfunkel”, for creating systems “designed to set fire to everything we value as human beings”, hasdirectly urged followersto speak out.Charlie Behrens of Wisconsinhas led a fight against datacenters in that state. His parody news broadcasts – warning it could soon be “goodbye, America’s dairyland and hello, America’s motherboard” – led to him headlining gatherings of hundreds.Sure, it may be “a little lofty to expect that your comedy could topple a billion-dollar corporation”, as Ross says. But we shouldn’t underestimate the power of comedy wielded en masse. Altman, the human face of ChatGPT, was recentlypresentedwith a clip of Husk,a former landscaperwho recently reached a million followers, asking the bot to time a supposed long-distance run, which it got wildly wrong. Altman appeared sheepish: “It’s a known issue.”Ross doesn’t believe comedians should be seen as philosophers, but it would be “wonderful”, he says, if humor “woke up an understanding in people’s minds that they’re also upset, and drove them toward questioning” our AI future.It’s easy to feel helpless against a tide of supposed robotic inevitability. But each small act of comedy offers permission to question our self-appointed AI overlords – a little win for the humans.Explore more on these topicsAI (artificial intelligence)ComedyAdvertisingfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Trump and Chinese president Xi end summit without major agreement on AI | AI (artificial intelligence) | The Guardian
description: Xi’s state visit to the US emphasized personal rapport with the US president, rather than substantial agreements to pause their respective countries’ AI arms race
Author: David Smith
Headline: Xi’s state visit to the US emphasized personal rapport with the US president, rather than substantial agreements to pause their respective countries’ AI arms race
Content: Donald Trump shakes hands with Chinese president Xi Jinping as they depart the National Archives Museum following a tour on 25 September.Photograph: Win McNamee/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenDonald Trump shakes hands with Chinese president Xi Jinping as they depart the National Archives Museum following a tour on 25 September.Photograph: Win McNamee/Getty ImagesAI (artificial intelligence)Trump and Chinese president Xi end summit without major agreement on AIXi’s state visit to the US emphasized personal rapport with the US president, rather than substantial agreements to pause their respective countries’ AI arms raceDavid Smithin WashingtonFri 25 Sep 2026 18.11 EDTLast modified on Fri 25 Sep 2026 18.13 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleDonald Trump and Chinese president Xi Jinping wrapped uptheir Washington summiton Friday, facing criticism that they had squandered an opportunity to pause their countries’ artificial intelligence (AI) arms race.The three-day state visit emphasised pageantry and personal rapport rather than substantial agreements. The US president and Xi discussed the wars in Iran and Ukraine and the status of Taiwan. Their biggest policy announcement was a modest two-month extension of a trade truce.But despite the presence of top tech executives ata White House state dinneron Thursday night, Trump and Xi failed to deliver the AI breakthrough that some experts and foreign governments had hoped for amid warnings that the technology could pose an existential threat to humanity.Diplomacy or ‘diplotainment’? Key takeaways from the Trump-Xi summit in WashingtonRead more“It was such a layup,” saidRo Khanna, the top Democrat on the House of Representatives’ select committee on China. “If [Trump] had just said, look, we have established technical working groups and we’ve agreed to a framework that has called for DeepSeek and Moonshot and Alibaba to sit down with Anthropic and OpenAI and Gemini and with technical experts and they’re going to commit to at least a pause on any self-improving AI, he could have looked like he was a statesman taking the lead.“I believeXi Jinpingwould have agreed to some of at least the technical working groups. But he [Trump] didn’t want to; he has no interest in doing that.”It wasthe first visit to the White Houseby a Chinese president in more than a decade and Xi’s second state visit to the US. Three days of pomp and circumstance culminated on Friday with Trump and Xi drinking tea. Trump said ⁠the summit ⁠had produced great strides and that “our ​farmers are going to be happy,” but did not provide details.The pair thenwent to the National Archives, where Trump and Xi looked at the original Declaration of Independence, the constitution and Bill of Rights. Trump told reporters they were comparing China’s documents to America’s founding documents. “Ours goes 250 years, which is great, and we’re proud of. Theirs goes 6,000 years. So there’s a little difference between 6,000 and 250. But we’re very proud of our 250.”On Thursday, Xi acknowledged that the US and China have the “responsibility to develop and manage AI for good” and “ensure that the development of AI is always ​under human control”. China aims to have next-generation smart terminals and AI agentsreach more than 90% penetrationby 2030.But Trump – who has repeatedly said the US must forge ahead to maintain its lead overChina– appeared more focused on his push to rebrand artificial intelligence as “super intelligence”, later claiming on social media that Xi “seems to like” the term without divulging the substance of their discussions.Later Trump hosteda black-tie state dinnerattended by titans of the tech industry. Bernie Sanders, an independent senator of Vermont,used social mediato label a photo of Trump and Xi’s table with guests’ net worth: Elon Musk of SpaceX and Tesla ($928bn), Lisa Su of Advanced Micro Devices ($3.5bn), Jensen Huang of Nvidia ($186bn) and Tim Cook of Apple ($3.1bn). Sanders commented: “A government of, by and for the billionaire class.”But their counterparts in the Chinese tech industry were not present and there was little sign of either country making even a symbolic gesture to apply the brakes.Khanna commented: “Trump didn’t have to have some groundbreaking treaty like Reagan and Gorbachev did [on nuclear weapons]. He could have at least said, look, we’re going to have a working group of Chinese and American technologists working together to make recommendations and enforcement and verification of the labs.”Jonathan Czin, a fellow in the China Center at the Brookings Institution thinktank in Washington, agrees that an opportunity was missed. “We are in this potentially transformative moment for both countries and for the world and for technology and, instead of having a meeting that would meet the moment, you got theatre of the absurd in lieu of that,” he said.“Even going into this meeting, you’re dealing with a septuagenarian and octogenarian who may or may not have ever had first-hand contact with actually using AI and what happens with this technology rests on their two shoulders. The only thing they seemed to agree about is that neither of them wants to slow down with this technology, regardless of their actual understanding of it.”The state visit underlinedthe contrast between Trump’s treatmentof democratic allies such as Canada and authoritarian rivals such as China. He broke from tradition to give Xi a red carpet welcome when he landed at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland.He also found time to show Xi around the White House, including a gallery wall of presidents where Joe Biden ismockingly depicted as an autopen, a construction site for his White House ballroom and a new helicopter landing pad. “He’s an expert on stone, aside from many other things, and he loves good granite,” Trump said.But the summit was somewhat overshadowed by Trump’s decision last week to bar CNN, MS Now and Politico from the White House, sparking a legal fight. On Thursday, Chinese state media were welcomed into the White House grounds even as members of America’s free press were frozen out, though later they gained entry. As in May,when Trump visited Beijing, the leaders did not hold a press conference.Czin of the Brookings Institution added: “I had very low expectations going into this meeting for anything of substance and the meeting managed to underwhelm even those low expectations. We went from the mezzanine down into the basement. In terms of the substance, it’s not clear to me what the US got out of this.”Senate Democrats also criticised the summit, arguing that Trump failed to secure meaningful concessions from Beijing on trade, security, human rights or AI.Chuck Schumer, the minority leader in the Senate,said: “As usual, Trump acts based solely on who flatters him at the moment, where the nearest photo op is, and what headline he covets. If you’re a foreign authoritarian, Trump won’t just invite you to visit America, he’ll greet you plane-side.”Trump and Xi are on track to meet twice more this year. In November, Xi will host the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China, and in December theGroup of 20 summitwill be held at the Trump National Doral Miami golf club in Florida.Explore more on these topicsAI (artificial intelligence)Donald TrumpXi JinpingUS foreign policyChinanewsShareReuse this content
